item.title: Archaeologists Near Alexandria Just Found A 115-Foot Party Boat Once Enjoyed By Ancient Egyptian Elites
item.description: Powered by 20 rowers, this massive vessel featured a central pavilion where the wealthy and powerful could, in the words of Greek historian Strabo, "dance without restraint and with extreme licentiousness." The post Archaeologists Near Alexandria Just Found A 115-Foot Party Boat Once Enjoyed By Ancient Egyptian Elites appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: Archaeologists In Virginia Have Uncovered Long-Lost Native American Settlements Described By John Smith In 1608
item.description: Thousands of Indigenous artifacts found along the Rappahannock River provide physical evidence of the villages written about by English explorer John Smith in 1608. The post Archaeologists In Virginia Have Uncovered Long-Lost Native American Settlements Described By John Smith In 1608 appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: Inside The Tragic Stories Of The Eight U.S. Presidents Who Have Died In Office
item.description: Four presidents have been assassinated, beginning with Abraham Lincoln in 1865, while others have died from heart attacks, strokes, and bacterial infections. The post Inside The Tragic Stories Of The Eight U.S. Presidents Who Have Died In Office appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: Archaeologists In France Just Found Two Ancient Roman ‘Piggy Banks’ Filled With 40,000 Coins
item.description: While excavating a settlement that was lost to a fire in the 4th century C.E., researchers found one storage jar filled with 23,000 coins weighing in at 83 pounds as well as another jar packed with 18,000 coins that weighed 110 pounds. The post Archaeologists In France Just Found Two Ancient Roman ‘Piggy Banks’ Filled With 40,000 Coins appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: Archaeologists In Turkey Just Discovered A Smiling Medusa Carved Into The Marble Ceiling Of An Ancient Walkway
item.description: The unusually cheerful depiction of Medusa was found carved onto a marble ceiling block in the ancient city of Amastris. item.title: Inside The Life And Death Of Shannon Hoon, The Troubled Lead Singer Of Blind Melon
item.description: Shannon Hoon was just 28 when he overdosed on cocaine in his band's tour bus after a years-long struggle with addiction. The post Inside The Life And Death Of Shannon Hoon, The Troubled Lead Singer Of Blind Melon appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: Archaeologists Believe They’ve Discovered The Earliest-Known Evidence Of Fire Made By Humans
item.description: Two little pieces of pyrite, also known as "fool's gold," that were unearthed at the Barnham archaeological site are the "smoking gun" proving that early humans were intentionally making fire as far back as 400,000 years ago. The post Archaeologists Believe They’ve Discovered The Earliest-Known Evidence Of Fire Made By Humans appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: Researchers Just Discovered A New Prehistoric Sea Cow Species That Lived 21 Million Years Ago
item.description: The now-extinct sea cow species, Salwasiren qatarensis, likely played a key role in its ocean ecosystems, much like modern-day dugongs. The post Researchers Just Discovered A New Prehistoric Sea Cow Species That Lived 21 Million Years Ago appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: The Chilling Story Of Serial Killer Robert Eugene Brashers, The Main Suspect In The 1991 Austin Yogurt Shop Murders
item.description: Twenty-six years after he died by suicide, DNA linked Robert Eugene Brashers to the quadruple homicide of four girls in Austin, Texas — as well as a number of other violent crimes. item.title: How Mark ‘Chopper’ Read Went From A Deadly Criminal To An Australian Folk Hero
item.description: "Chopper" Read was a mob enforcer and contract killer who prided himself on only bringing harm to fellow criminals — then he became a bestselling author while still behind bars after writing a memoir about his deadly exploits.
